item.title: State of pause?
item.description: Donald Trump says he has postponed a planned attack on Iran at the request of Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Does this mean real negotiations and diplomacy are being taken seriously? Or does this mean Trump has no idea how to end a war he started? CrossTalking with Marwa Osman, Ali Alizadeh, and Haytham Faraj.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Drone wars
item.description: Up the escalation ladder: Will the presence of Ukrainian drones in the skies over the Baltic States bring about a direct Russia-NATO conflict? We should all be worried. Also, will the fiasco now known as the Iran War find its final destination in Cuba. CrossTalking with George Szamuely and Mark Sleboda.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Insults as strategy
item.description: Theatrics is not a substitute for strategy. Zelensky’s insulting letter to the Russian president is a reflection of the West’s inability to negotiate in good faith. Also, Germany’s denial of a seat on the UN Security Council demonstrates Berlin’s fading importance in the world. This can also be said of Europe in general. CrossTalking with Mark Sleboda and George Szamuely.

item.title: Peace without peace
item.description: Wars are easy to start but very difficult to end. Donald Trump is learning this the hard way. The American president is clearly looking for an exit from this conflict. His partner in this war is Israel. Israel has very different ideas. CrossTalking with Raed Jarrar, Elijah J. Magnier, and Hamidreza Gholamzadeh.

item.title: Economic spiral
item.description: The longer the war on Iran continues, the more damage will be inflicted on the global economy. This is not only about energy and fertilizers, but also about global supply chains. Once interrupted or broken, the nature of the global order could be fundamentally altered. How we come out of this is anyone’s guess. CrossTalking with Alam Saleh, Max Ajl, and Mario Arturo Ruiz Estrada.

item.title: Losing control
item.description: Wars are unpredictable – the ultimate exercise in the law of unintended consequences. The Americans and Israelis have realized this and are in a state of panic. The Iranians, on the other hand, are playing their asymmetrical hand masterfully. CrossTalking with Larry Johnson, Jason Zaharis, and Esteban Carrillo Lopez.
